body_markdown:
**DALLAS** (November 18, 2026) — AECOM (NYSE: ACM), the trusted global infrastructure leader, today announced it has been selected by the[Delta Conveyance Design and Construction Authority](https://dcdca.org/) (DCA) to provide programmatic geotechnical exploration and reporting services for the[Delta Conveyance Project](https://www.deltaconveyanceproject.com/) (DCP), which is intended to modernize California’s State Water Project by improving the reliability and resilience of water deliveries for approximately 27 million Californians.


“As California faces growing pressures from climate change, sea level rise and aging infrastructure, investments in resilient water systems are more important than ever,” said Beverley Stinson, chief executive of AECOM’s global Water business. “Through this work, our teams will provide the geotechnical data and engineering insight needed to support informed decision-making throughout project development. We are honored to bring our number one-ranked global water expertise to an initiative that will help strengthen California’s water system for generations to come.”


Under a five-year contract as the Exploration Consultant, AECOM is expected to lead and manage large-scale geotechnical and geoenvironmental investigations, laboratory testing, engineering data development, and reporting to support this critical initiative. AECOM has supported the Delta Conveyance Project since 2009, providing geotechnical, geologic, engineering and program management services across key phases of project development. The work spans portions of Sacramento, San Joaquin, Contra Costa and Alameda counties and is expected to generate the subsurface understanding and engineering insight needed to inform project planning, reduce risk, and support the reliable delivery of critical water infrastructure for California communities.


“The Delta Conveyance Project is one of the most significant infrastructure investments in California in the last 50 years, requiring a combination of deep technical expertise, regional understanding and proven program delivery experience,” said Matt Crane, president and chief operating officer of AECOM’s U.S. & Latin America region. “With more than 15 years of involvement supporting this project, our team brings industry-leading geotechnical capabilities, a strong local presence, and the resources needed to execute complex investigations at scale. We are proud to continue supporting the DCA as it advances this critical project to help strengthen the long-term resilience of California’s water infrastructure.”


AECOM’s geotechnical investigation is expected to provide information for the safe design and construction of conveyance facilities while helping minimize impacts to Delta communities, agriculture and sensitive ecosystems. By advancing a more comprehensive understanding of subsurface conditions and potential risks, the work mitigates risks to California’s water systems, including sea level rise, saltwater intrusion and seismic events.


**About AECOM**


AECOM (NYSE: ACM) is the global infrastructure leader, committed to delivering a better world. As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $15.1 billion in fiscal year 2026. Learn more at[aecom.com](http://aecom.com/) .
